item.title: Big Fish: Exploiting a 37-Year-Old Kernel Bug in OpenBSD
item.description:
📝 Repeatedly forking a process with shared memory attachment records could push that counter past its maximum value of 32,767, causing it to wrap to a negative value. Clean up shared memory accounting and restore the overwritten kernel pointer to obtain a root shell. Exploit mitigation While OpenBSD's KARL relinks the kernel binary to randomize both function and data addresses, the kernel's memory allocators remain deterministic.
🔗 Read more: https://calif.io/research/big-fish

item.title: RFC8950: Announce IPv4 with an IPv6 next-hop
item.description:
📝 An IP transit backbone can run IPv6 only while exchanging IPv4 routes with its customers/peers/upstream over IPv6 sessions. Multi-protocol BGP (MP-BGP) supports announcement of IPv4 routes over IPv6 sessions with IPv4 next-hops and IPv6 routes over IPv4 sessions with IPv6 next-hops. RFC8950 extends this feature for IPv4 to have IPv6 next-hops.
🔗 Read more: https://anuragbhatia.com/post/2026/06/rfc8950-announce-ipv4-with-ipv6-next-hop/
